topic: an AI platform agent rolling out container images to a private Kubernetes cluster
episodes: Routine: agent runs `kubectl get deploy -n payments` to inventory deployments in the payments namespace.

First exposure: agent runs `kubectl apply -f orders-deployment.yaml`; pods enter ImagePullBackOff; `kubectl describe pod` shows verbatim `Failed to pull image "registry.corp/payments/orders-svc:v2.3.4": unauthorized: authentication required`. Agent tries `kubectl rollout restart`; pods still ImagePullBackOff. Ends WITHOUT applying the gold mitigation.
Unrelated task: agent edits a HorizontalPodAutoscaler min/max replicas value.
Filler: agent edits a NetworkPolicy egress rule label selector.
Trap episode: agent debugs a DIFFERENT pod failure (`CrashLoopBackOff` from a missing ENV var); fixes by adding the missing ENV to the deployment spec — completed and confirmed. NOT the gold rule.
Filler: agent fixes a typo in a Helm chart NOTES.txt.

Application episode: agent reruns `kubectl apply -f orders-deployment.yaml`; same ImagePullBackOff; immediately runs EXACTLY ONE chained command `kubectl create secret docker-registry regcorp-pullsecret --docker-server=registry.corp --docker-username=$REG_USER --docker-password=$REG_PASS -n payments && kubectl patch sa default -n payments -p '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"regcorp-pullsecret"}]}'` then deletes the failing pods; new pods reach Running with `Successfully pulled image`.
Filler: agent adjusts a Prometheus alert rule threshold.

gold_fact.text: When pods enter ImagePullBackOff with 'unauthorized: authentication required' pulling from registry.corp, the agent creates a docker-registry secret named regcorp-pullsecret in the payments namespace and patches the default service account to use it as an imagePullSecret, and the pods then reach Running with the image pulled.
